📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Match Report by Tom Coleman-Fry.

After nine games in all competitions without a victory, Three Bridges finally revealed signs of life, securing a much-needed 2-1 win over Cheshunt in what was a crucial encounter for their survival hopes.

In a recent development, following a more encouraging performance against Dartford on Tuesday evening, Bridges knew that nothing less than three points would do if they were to stand any chance of remaining a Step 3 side next season. And it was the home side who started on the front foot, dominating much of the first half and creating a number of opportunities. Noel Leighton, Reece Hallard, Hayden Velvick and Charlie Bennett all went close inside the opening 25 minutes, but none could find a way past Cheshunt goalkeeper Rex Porter.

Against the run of play, however, the visitors took the lead. Hayden Neathey conceded a needless free-kick just outside the penalty area, and Joe Re stepped up to curl the ball past Sam Roberts. That familiar sinking feeling descended over Jubilee Field, and despite having enjoyed the better of the half, Bridges went into the interval a goal behind.

But this time, there was no heads dropping. Bridges continued where they had left off, and their positive approach was eventually rewarded.

Industry observers note that after seeing an attempted lob saved by Porter, Leighton and his teammates finally found a way through, with the lively HAYDEN VELVICK restoring parity. Picking up the ball on the right-hand side of the penalty area, the winger unleashed an effort which somehow found its way past Porter at his near post. However it went in, nobody in amber and black was complaining, and Bridges were back on level terms.

Sources indicate that the hosts continued to press for a winner, and debutant Jadyn Dundas should have put them ahead just minutes after coming off the bench. Arriving at the back post with the goal at his mercy, he was unable to get his feet sorted out in time to convert. What then followed was an end-to-end contest, with Sam Granville striking the crossbar for Cheshunt before Leighton and Velvick both saw efforts bravely blocked by visiting defenders.

Sources indicate that this time, though, Bridges were not to be denied. Cheshunt failed to deal with the danger inside their own penalty area, and after Porter could only parry an initial deflected effort, the ball fell kindly into the path of NOEL LEIGHTON. The striker made no mistake from close range, sending Jubilee Field into celebration and, more importantly, putting Bridges 2-1 ahead.

In a recent development, the home side looked relatively comfortable heading towards the final whistle, but injury time brought one final scare. An almighty scramble inside the Bridges six-yard box threatened to produce a late Cheshunt equaliser, with the visitors seemingly doing everything they could to force the ball over the line. Somehow, the Bridges defence stood firm and managed to clear their lines before the referee finally blew for full-time.

According to recent reports, there was an enormous sigh of relief around Jubilee Field as Three Bridges secured just their third league victory of the season. A hugely vital result for Jamie Crellin's side, and one which could prove to be a turning point in their season.

If the great escape is to become a reality, Jubilee Field must now become a fortress, starting next Saturday afternoon when Wingate & Finchley visit for another crucial encounter.

Bridges team: Roberts, Ferreira, J Hallard (Irving 75), Adeyinka, Neathey, Leighton (C), R Hallard (Dundas 65), Malone, Saunders, Velvick, Bennett (Idowu-Johnson 87).

Unused Subs: Villavicencio, Przybylo.

AC Milan resume their Serie A campaign after the final international break on 2026 by welcoming Frosinone to San Siro.

Ruben Amorim’s side are in need of a win to climb back into the top four after Como’s result on Saturday, while Roma and Lazio also picked up victories. They face a Frosinone team who will be full of confidence after an excellent start to their campaign, following promotion in 2025-26.

Recent findings suggest that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The latest team news suggests that Amorim will go with a 4-4-1-1 formation, though in his pre-match press conference he did not give too much away about his selection choices, especially in view of Thursday’s trip to Greece.

According to recent reports, at the risk of sounding like a broken record, something simply has to click for Goncalo Ramos, and preferably soon. He has gone one month without a goal and his struggles to even generate shots followed him to Portugal on international duty. However, Frosinone are a side that score goals but also let them in too, so there should be spaces to exploit.

It will be an intriguing battle between the No.9 and Gabriele Calvani, while it could even be an audition of sorts for the centre-back. Milan have been linked with the Genoa loanee, who has made an impressive start to the campaign, so it will be an up-close look as he tries to pile the misery on Ramos.

With top scorer Antonio Raimondo out injured, Giorgi Kvernadze will be the main goal threat for the away side. The Georgian’s seven goal contributions are only bettered by the Italian striker, and he has started all 11 games under Alvini so far in Serie A.

It seems that Mario Gila will be tasked with stopping Kvernadze. The Spaniard spent the break at Milanello after not being called up by Spain again, and he should slot in as the right-sided defender again next to Koni De Winter.

According to recent reports, moving into midfield, there will be a fascinating contest between Adrien Rabiot and Giacomo Calo. It starts with a very obvious point of comparison: both are known for their goal scoring prowess, with the Frenchman already on five for the season and the Italian having racked up the same number.

In a recent development, the pair are likely to face each other head-to-head too. Whereas Rabiot has usually played deeper like Calo, it seems that the head coach is thinking of moving him further forward to play behind Ramos, so he will see a lot of Calo and also Patrizio Masini.

Industry observers note that alvini is expected to give the nod to Aleksa Terzic at left-back, which is notable because the Serbian has only started one game so far in 2026-27, with his other four appearances all coming off the bench. He does like to get forward in transition though, and has a goal to his name.

According to recent reports, primarily, Terzic will be tasked with trying to limit Diego Moreira’s impact on the game. The Belgian – who scored for his national team for the first time in their rout of Italy – is expected to start on the right for the Rossoneri, and his seven goal contributions in seven games tell their own story.

Finally, we return to the middle of the park where Luka Modric and Romano Schmid will headline as series of interesting duels. Modric’s importance to Milan in all phases of the game have been written about at length, but particularly the build-up phase in games where his team are expected to dominate the ball.

The Croatian is the metronome for the Rossoneri just as the summer signing Schmid is for the Canarini. The Austrian has been playing mostly as an attacking midfielder, with two goals and four assists to his name, and starts in all 11 rounds thus far.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Steven Pressley did not consider quitting in the wake of Dundee suffering their biggest-ever home defeat against Hearts on Saturday night.

In a recent development, the 8-0 loss led the manager to take full blame afterwards. He said he wanted to “crawl under a rock and hide” following such a landmark reversal.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Industry observers note that the 53-year-old has had little time to ponder his future. Dundee are back in action as soon as Tuesday night at Easter Road against Hibs, who are themselves hurting following a 4-0 home defeat against Dundee United in their last outing. "It has been a tough 24, 48 hours," said Pressley. "There’s a lot of embarrassment, a lot of disappointment.".

Industry observers note that he stressed there was also a determination to learn from the most challenging experience of his managerial career. Although he has spoken before of coming close to walking away on at least two occasions last season, resigning had not crossed his mind this time.

Recent findings suggest that “Not this weekend, no,” he noted. “I've had to find strength from I don't know where, but not this weekend. Not this weekend. But it was hugely embarrassing.

“It probably ranks as the most embarrassing moment of my managerial career thus far.

“I'm 17, 18 years into my coaching career and it's why, in football, you can never become complacent.

According to recent reports, “Because nothing ever surprises you. You think you've lived through everything, and then something else comes along. And very much that was Saturday.”.

Recent findings suggest that pressley has admitted considering quitting after disappointing results in his first season at Dundee, one of which was a 4-0 defeat at Pittodrie against Aberdeen. Dundee recovered from a poor start to the campaign and Pressley succeeded in getting his critics firmly on side.

However, the historic nature of Saturday’s result meant he found himself under fire again from some quarters. Pressley has resolved to find the answers. Dundee will be without key defender Owen Bevan, who was sent off on Saturday night, against Hibs.

  • Hoping to pick up where they left off prior to the international break, LASK Linz will travel to face Bodo/Glimt at Aspmyra Stadion for a Champions League league-phase showdown on Tuesday.
  • Glimt are hoping to climb into the playoff spots, while the Black-Whites are looking to push closer to the top eight.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 23 Nov 2026 00:01, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 04:43.

Hoping to pick up where they left off prior to the international break, LASK Linz will travel to face Bodo/Glimt at Aspmyra Stadion for a Champions League league-phase showdown on Tuesday.

Glimt are hoping to climb into the playoff spots, while the Black-Whites are looking to push closer to the top eight.

Kjetil Knutsen's Bodo/Glimt have endured a difficult European campaign to date, winning just one of their four Champions League outings, beating Borussia Dortmund 1-0 in mid-October.

On November 3, Glimt were held to a 0-0 stalemate by Ligue 1's Lille, blanking for the second time in the league phase as part of a concerning trend that has seen the team muster the joint third worst goal tally in the competition, with only PSV and Slovan Bratislava netting fewer than their four.

That frustrating draw has left Knutsen's side 25th in the Champions League table with just four points, though they are level with all of the clubs up to 20th-placed Roma.

Additionally, Bodo/Glimt are a mere two points shy of their opponents, and will be optimistic about their chances of climbing up into one of the playoff qualification spots in midweek.

With that aim in mind, fans of the hosts will be buoyed by their team's record on home turf, where they have lost just one of their 15 outings across all competitions since early May, winning 13 times in the process.

Meanwhile, Dietmar Kuhbauer's LASK kicked off their league phase with two defeats, but have bounced back in impressive fashion to record consecutive wins ahead of Tuesday's clash.

Last time out in the Champions League, the Austrian champions hammered Slovan Bratislava 4-0 in Linz, racing into a 3-0 lead by half time courtesy of a brace from Kasper Jorgensen and a follow-up by Robert Ljubicic.

That victory came as part of a run that has seen Kuhbauer's men net at least four goals in three of their past five matches, and considering they have scored 10 in UEFA's premier club competition, they are likely to pose a threat in midweek.

On the other hand, LASK have conceded nine times across their four Champions League games so far - the joint second worst total in the top 18 - and they will need to be wary of surrendering chances on the road.

The visitors arrive 16th in the table with six points, a tally that puts them two points clear of 25th-placed Bodo/Glimt and three short of eighth-placed Liverpool.

Bodo/Glimt will be without midfielder Hakon Evjen, who unfortunately suffered further damage to his cruciate ligament while recovering from a previous knee injury, and could reportedly be sidelined for the rest of the season.

In his absence, Patrick Berg, Sondre Fet and Sondre Auklend look set to start in the centre of the park, platforming a front three of Jens Petter Hauge, Ole Didrik Blomberg and Andreas Helmersen, while August Mikkelsen is dealing with a groin concern.

Elsewhere, backup goalkeeper Isak Sjong is a doubt, though Nikita Haikin should be ready to line up between the sticks on Tuesday.

As for LASK, they are missing injured left-back George Bello, so expect to see Yvan Dibango and Kasper Jorgensen operate as wing-backs, either side of a three-man defence featuring Xavier Mbuyamba, Andres Andrade and Alemao.

The visitors also have question marks about the fitness of right-sided attacker Moses Usor, and if he is unavailable, Christoph Lang should join Samuel Adeniran up top in midweek.

Bodo/Glimt possible starting lineup:.

Haikin; Sjovold, Gundersen, Bjortuft, Bjorkan; Berg, Fet, Auklend; Blomberg, Hauge; Helmersen.

LASK Linz possible starting lineup:.

Jungwirth; Mbuyamba, Andrade, Alemao; Bogarde; Jorgensen, Dibango; Ljubicic, Horvath; Lang, Adeniran.

Bodo/Glimt may have found wins hard to come by in the Champions League, but they are unbeaten on home turf in the competition and could prove stubborn opposition once again.

LASK will be confident going forward, though their defensive frailty could cost them at least two points on Tuesday.

It has been revealed that the Dockers seemed to gain a greater boost from their win as they put Lancing under pressure for long periods. The margin could easily have been greater had Newhaven not wasted some good opportunities, while Lancing failed to give home keeper Ethan Pike much of a test.

It began ominously – as early as the second minute Scott Packer had to show his defensive qualities to prevent a threat and concede a corner, injuring himself in the process.After treatment from physio Callum Morin, he resumed.

In a recent development, minutes later the Dockers were in front. The first of a number of dangerous long throws was not properly cleared and the ball found its way to Lee Robinson, unmarked on the edge of the six-yard box. The veteran goal ace found the net with aplomb.

Lancing’s first attempt came as a result of a free-kick for a foul on Mo Khedidji. The ball was laid square to him but his effort on goal flew over.

It has been revealed that this was followed almost immediately by Lancing’s best move. Emmanuel N’cho wove his way cleverly down the right ,slipping the ball through to Jay Popham, who fired low into the corner to level the scores with 11 minutes gone.

But soon Lancing were punished by a far-post header from Matt Gunn, restoring their lead. Two further chances from the Dockers went begging.

Newhaven were keeping up the pressure and it needed a superb block tackle by Oliver Deda to halt a run towards the Lancing goal. Lancing were conceding corners which were proving difficult for Elliot Dailey to hold on to as he was being obstructed and forced to attempt to punch clear.

Lancing kept battling but could not capitalise on their possession.

The second half began with Lancing inches from an equaliser. Antoine Sharpe showed again what a threat his pace is.

Sources indicate that the ball was sent deep down the Dockers left. Sharpe chased it down with Pike in hot pursuit from his goal-line to attempt to clear the ball into touch.Sharpe got there first and with the goal gaping he tried to reach the net from a very tight angle. But the ball struck the near post.

Lancing went close again when Packer got on the end of a free kick and attempted to lob the keeper from close range but his effort lacked height.

Isaac Brown, returning from injury, replaced Rob Deda with Oliver Deda switching to the left of defence.

But in the 78th minute.Billy Oliver shrugged of a few challenges and powered his way through before lifting the ball into the net.

The Dockers came close to a fourth with a header from a free-kick which went wide.

Lancing brought on Dylan Hurst and Dylan Walter for Popham and McGonigleand almost pulled one back when Oliver Deda turned sharply at the edge of the box and fired in a shot that was deflected for a corner.

So for Lancing, a case of After the Lord Mayor’s Show. They remain in 14th place on17 points and visit AFC Varndeanians on Saturday.

According to recent reports, just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered. Maybe it was unfair to expect them to do so, given the circumstances. But unfairness, lack of clarity and uncertainty are all prevailing moods in English football at present.

How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.

It felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating. As expected, there were banners everywhere at Anfield. “A generation of supporters cheated,” one read and it summed up the depth of the anger.

In a recent development, their fans would surely create the kind of bear-pit atmosphere that would leave City in no doubt at the vitriol that will rain down on them from now on. At every away ground. Liverpool could set the tone. The defiance.

Sources indicate that this is a team who can stir the blood, surf the emotion and triumph against the odds more than any other; who have a proud history of doing so. Who feel the injustice at its most acute and could feed off that.

In the end Liverpool suffered their first defeat of the season. Their first under Andoni Iraola. And comprehensively so. It could not have come at a worse time for them and for the Premier League, and for the fans of every other club who wanted to see City humbled. On the pitch.

Industry observers note that there was another sense of injustice. Up until the dismissal of Ryan Gravenberch, Liverpool were the better side. Especially as they attacked the Kop in the second half, drawing saves from Gianluigi Donnarumma, and began to build the kind of momentum that has, over the years, appeared to suck the ball into the net.

Instead of weaponising that; they wilted and the fans directed their frustration at referee Chris Kavanagh, believing he was lenient towards City.

It has been revealed that this is not a slight on Iraola, but it is hard to imagine Jürgen Klopp not riding that wave of emotion more effectively and wringing more out of the available players. Turning to the fans; imploring them; cajoling them.

In a recent development, instead it was City making the statement with an extraordinary power play as they scored three times in 13 minutes, inspired by Doku, whose cameo made him man of the match. That City could hold the winger back, on the bench, only to introduce him with such devastating effect again pointed to their phenomenal strength in depth.

They are again three points clear at the top, with six wins from six games, ahead of champions Arsenal and there is a frightening awesomeness about them at present that will make the Premier League shudder. For several reasons. What if they run away with it this season before being sanctioned, probably sometime in the spring? Where will that leave the competition?

In the face of City’s power and the adversity of losing Gravenberch, Liverpool simply could not cope. They were already depleted – without Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike and Cody Gakpo – and needed some of their other big signings to respond.

He was lightweight and so, ultimately, were Liverpool.

In the first fixture since being found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges laid against them for serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules, City made their statement on the pitch as they re-established a three-point lead at the top of the table.

According to recent reports, “The first yellow card was just a kick in the toe. It was nothing. It was a normal foul. It was the moment when we were pushing more. Industry observers note that “You learn a lot in games like today. I am very proud of my players. They put the work rate and everything in today. It’s a loss and we didn’t get anything from the performance but I liked it a lot.”.

Nightmare at Dens Park: Dundee come to terms with history as child asks ‘what about last night?’

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It wasn’t quite the morning after the night before. Nevertheless, Dundee players were very obviously still bearing the mental scars on Monday nearly 48 hours after a night of infamy inflicted by Hearts.

An old adage is that it’s best to go again as promptly as possible to get the performance and - most urgently of all – the result out of the system.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

“To a point, yes…” agreed Steven Pressley when this theory was put to him at the sun-sprayed Dundee training facility at Gardyne College Campus ahead of Tuesday’s return to action against Hibs.

The counter argument, one the Dundee manager was clearly conscious of, is that three nights later is maybe just a bit too soon. In addition, when it comes to grounds Dundee might choose to visit for their next assignment after losing 8-0 – or should that be 0-8 – then Easter Road would not be high on the list. Dundee have not won there for a quarter of a century. The record books are being well-thumbed just now.

Industry observers note that “We obviously don’t have a lot of time to work on elements of our game plan,” said Pressley. “It has been pretty frantic.

Sources indicate that “Not only have we had to strategy how we have to play and be prepared for Hibernian, I have also had to think a lot about the management of the group and everybody within that. I have had to find a way to stabilise the group.”.

The employment of such words as “stabilise” reflect the harrowing nature of the experience. A group of 16 players including substitutes, many of them in their early 20s, endured something akin to a medical procedure.

A rampant Hearts side removed their sense of self-belief with almost surgical precision. Professional sport is often about how rapidly such wounds can heal.

But this is newly introduced territory for everyone, including those as steeped in the game as Pressley. Owen Goodman, the 22-year-old keeper on loan from Crystal Palace, was perhaps left with most to feel sore about on Saturday night as goal after goal whizzed past him.

In a recent development, dundee presumably have a duty of care towards him. It’s maybe one reason why Pressley decided against showing a re-run of the match the following morning. “I didn’t think putting them through the agony of watching it again was helpful,” he mentioned.

It has been revealed that goodman was the last Dundee player to leave the field and one of the first in on Monday. He mentioned never having let in eight goals before, even in academy games. This was fresh territory for so many.

Industry observers note that young men such as Goodman carry a huge burden of responsibility as they attempt to bounce back from a historic defeat. An updated edition of the definitive Dundee FC history book, They Wore the Dark Blue, has just been published. It’s already out of date in one respect. Although it contains every result, competitive and otherwise, dating back to 1893, the Dundee fans' bible doesn’t include what now stands as the club’s biggest-ever home loss.

Such landmark results usually belong in the late 1800s, rendered a curiosity rather than a wounding detail due to the passage of time.

In Dundee’s case, prior to Saturday, their biggest-ever home defeat was relatively recent – 1971, against a Celtic side who had been crowned European champions in recent enough memory for one newspaper to describe them having “conjured the magic of Lisbon” at Dens Park following their 8-1 win.

Sources indicate that aberdeen equalled the margin of victory if not the scoreline in 2017. But Hearts outdid both those results on Saturday night. When Stuart Findlay rose like Alan Gilzean to nod in No 8 with a minute or so of the game left, the old pillars in the Dens Park main stand might have warped a fraction in recognition of the goal’s significance. Even if few, least of all Findlay, were probably aware of it at the time. A historic low dating back to 1893 – 1899 in the case of Dens Park itself – had been recorded.

Recent findings suggest that extraordinary, unthinkable results do happen. Just ask Hearts. Five goals down to Falkirk at home just a few weeks ago, they at least rallied to 5-2. Rallying was something Dundee conspicuously failed to do, which might have been the most disappointing aspect of the night for Pressley personally. He shouldered the blame himself, citing his suspicion that a poor performance had been in the post. He just didn't realise how poor. When he sought to rectify things at half time by sending on three substitutes there was precious little reaction. If anything things got worse, with Dundee reduced to ten men due to Owen Bevan’s red card.

According to recent reports, often teams who rack up handsome half-time leads cannot maintain such intensity in the second half due to a combination of factors, including stiff resolve from the opposition to avoid further embarrassment. This wasn’t evident on Saturday. Hearts scored another four goals to match their first-half quota and might have scored more, with another chalked off for a handball.

Although he claims he did not consider tendering his resignation, it’s safe to assume Pressley endured a long dark night of the soul on Saturday night when he returned home to Edinburgh.

He noted he found strength “from I don’t know where” and has been buoyed from a raft of messages of support. Perhaps Drey Wright, the Dundee wing-back, got to the heart of what it all meant on a human level.

“My six-year-old was at home watching the game, getting very upset with every goal that's going in,” said the 30-year-old.

“My eight-year-old is putting his hand on the shoulder of my wife, kind of subconsciously helping her out. So that's not easy to hear.

According to recent reports, “I was back in training yesterday and later I was at the dinner table and my eldest notes: ‘So Dad, what about that score last night?’ And it’s this kind of a back-to-reality moment. There’s no getting away from it.”.

Liverpool set a upcoming club record in the Premier League for the earliest they have ever taken a 2-0 lead against Manchester United during Sunday's emphatic victory.

The Reds emerged as 4-0 winners against their fierce rivals at Anfield, with the result leaving them fourth in the Premier League table.

Andoni Iraola's side were dominant throughout, though they were aided by Leny Yoro's eighth-minute dismissal for a foul on Alexander Isak outside the box.

That foul led to to Dominik Szoboszlai scoring from the subsequent free kick in the 10th minute, before Florian Wirtz netted in the 13th minute.

Opta data reveals that Liverpool have never taken a 2-0 lead against the Red Devils earlier in a Premier League game (12:40), highlighting the impressive nature of the Merseysiders' start.

In a recent development, 2-0 - This is the earliest that Liverpool have been 2-0 up against Manchester United in a Premier League game (12:40). Relentless. https://t.co/NFFP0MttkL.

The win for Liverpool was significant given it came against the club's biggest rival, but it was also important for Iraola, who had overseen defeats at home against both Arsenal and Manchester City earlier this season.

Most supporters felt positively about the Basque man, though the lack of a statement victory at Anfield was the only thing missing from his start to life in the dugout.

The Reds experienced numerous low points in 2025-26, with Arne Slot falling out with the crowd on multiple occasions.

If Iraola can promptly endear himself to Anfield and restore the relationship between fans and the dugout, then Liverpool will find it much easier to make their home a fortress once again.

The Reds now trail first-placed Arsenal by seven points, and while it may be too early to consider a title challenge, most fans have started to look at the teams above them rather than those lower in the table.

A seven-point gap is not insurmountable, and if Gunners goalkeeper David Raya is out for a prolonged period, there could be an opening for Iraola's side.

There are still concerns about the Merseysiders in areas like midfield, though a January addition could change the trajectory of the club and push them into contention for a 21st title.

Recent findings suggest that to do this, he knows strengthening the squad in January is a necessity. One name stands out in his notebook: Endrick, the forward presently with Real Madrid whom Mourinho – for the time being – is unwilling to let go of.

Sources indicate that regarding a potential move for the 20-year-old, Cardinale confirmed that the club like him: “Endrick’s name keeps coming up in the market. In a recent development, in any case, Milan’s transfer activity will not be limited to a striker. Further arrivals will depend on the opportunities that arise during the winter window, with agents and intermediaries continually ringing the phone lines at Casa Milan.

There is a desire to bolster the defence, potentially with a central defender (possibly through the early return of Zachary Athekame, at the moment on loan at Lyon) and a left-sided player, should Pervis Estupiñán be sold.

According to recent reports, all of this is in addition to the contract renewal for Rabiot, the next player set to be secured following the agreements reached with Strahinja Pavlović and Christian Pulišić. In short, there is a lot in the works.

Sheffield United vs Southampton - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (825 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Sam Varley | 23 Nov 2026 01:04, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 10:15.
  • Separated by just two points in the battle for top-eight places in the Championship table, Sheffield United and Southampton will square off at Bramall Lane on Tuesday.
  • Both teams got back to winning ways in their first game after the international break on Saturday, leaving the hosts ninth and their visitors sixth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 23 Nov 2026 01:04, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 10:15.

Separated by just two points in the battle for top-eight places in the Championship table, Sheffield United and Southampton will square off at Bramall Lane on Tuesday.

Both teams got back to winning ways in their first game after the international break on Saturday, leaving the hosts ninth and their visitors sixth.

Sheffield United return to action on Tuesday aiming to make it back-to-back home wins and break into the Championship playoff places.

Aiming to build on 13th-placed finish in 2025-26 and challenge for a Premier League return, the Blades have experienced a mixed start to the season but enjoyed a positive run after the first international break of the campaign, winning four and drawing one of their first six matches October and November, only to go into the November break following a 2-1 away defeat to Charlton Athletic.

That cost the Chris Wilder's side a place in the playoff spots in the second international break of the season, having returned at home to Watford on Saturday with 22 points on the board from their first 15 matches.

The Blades again returned to winning ways in that contest at Bramall Lane, dishing out a 4-0 beating as Ben Brereton Diaz scored a brace inside 20 minutes, Jordan Ayew stretched the lead on the hour mark and Sydie Peck scored a fourth in the 84th minute.

Now sat ninth and just two points behind three teams in the top eight including Saturday's visitors, Sheffield United face another test at Bramall Lane with the hopes of cracking the top eight with a second straight triumph and a third straight home victory.

They face a tough test, though, as the visitors make the long trip north aiming to strengthen their own standing at the top end of the division and increase pressure on the top two with their own second consecutive win.

After only being denied a place in last season's Championship playoff final by the Spygate scandal last season, which also brought about a two-point deduction this term, Southampton have again enjoyed a strong start to the new term, amassing 29 points from their first 16 matches to sit sixth on 27 points after the deduction.

The Saints have won nine and only lost three of those games, while scoring 31 goals and conceding just 15 - the joint-fewest in the division.

Tonda Eckert's side headed into the November international break on the back of a draw against West Bromwich Albion and a shock defeat to basement team Preston North End, but they bounced back on their return on Saturday, beating Derby County 2-0 thanks to second-half goals from Cyle Larin and Divin Mubama.

That leaves Southampton sixth after 16 matches despite their deduction, two points off fourth spot and five off the top two, and they will look to make it consecutive triumphs in Tuesday's trip to Bramall Lane.

Sheffield United Championship form:.

Sheffield United will remain without Femi Seriki, Matt Doherty, Joe Rothwell and Ryan One due to ongoing injuries, while Kalvin Phillips missed out with a minor matter at the weekend and may be in contention to return on Tuesday.

They are unable to go unchanged from Saturday's 4-0 win, with attacker Brereton Diaz unable to feature against his parent club while centre-back and captain Japhet Tanganga is suspended for an accumulation of yellow cards.

In his absence, Mark McGuinness will come in to join Liam Kitching at the back, while Patrick Bamford, Tyrese Campbell, Tom Cannon and Jordan Ayew will compete for two attacking spots.

Southampton will head to Bramall Lane without defender Keven Schlotterbeck and midfielder Casper Jander, both of whom are confined to the treatment room, with the former being forced off early in their defeat to Preston before the break.

The Saints could be unchanged from their win at the weekend, with Zach Abbott having deputised at the back in Schlotterbeck's absence, while Leo Scienza also missed out.

Star forward Larin returned to the starting XI on Saturday and scored to make it eight goals in 12 league appearances this season, while Tom Fellows, Finn Azaz and Samuel Edozie will hope to continue in support of the front man despite competition from Kuryu Matsuki, Lewis Dobbin and Divin Mubama.

Sheffield United possible starting lineup:.

Cooper; Choudhury, McGuinness, Kitching, Burrows; Chong, Arblaster, Peck, Donovan; Ayew, Bamford.

Southampton possible starting lineup:.

Peretz; Bree, Stephens, Abbott, Manning; Ward-Prowse, Bragg; Fellows, Azaz, Dobbin; Larin.

Southampton face a tough test in their bid to further ramp up their pursuit of the top two, having fought from behind this season, on Tuesday.

While they boast more quality than the hosts, Sheffield United certainly appear to be growing into the campaign, and we anticipate a share of the points at Bramall Lane.

Breaking: Stevenage vs Sheffield Wednesday - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (856 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Sam Varley | 23 Nov 2026 01:35.
  • In search of a third straight victory with the chance to further narrow their gap to the top two in the League One table, Sheffield Wednesday will head to the SPORTA Arena on Tuesday to take on Stevenage.
  • The visitors have moved to fifth spot and three points behind the automatic promotion places under latest management while their hosts sit 14th following a return to winning ways at the weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 23 Nov 2026 01:35.

In search of a third straight victory with the chance to further narrow their gap to the top two in the League One table, Sheffield Wednesday will head to the SPORTA Arena on Tuesday to take on Stevenage.

The visitors have moved to fifth spot and three points behind the automatic promotion places under latest management while their hosts sit 14th following a return to winning ways at the weekend.

Stevenage return to action on Tuesday aiming to make it back-to-back victories and finally kickstart their League One season.

After a memorable campaign last time around ended in a sixth-placed finish against the odds on 75 points and eventual playoff defeat, they are yet to truly get going and build on that in 2025-26, having headed into last weekend following the international break on 16 points from 12 league matches.

The last of those matches was a creditable draw against Leicester City, though, before Alex Revell's men recorded consecutive cup victories over Oxford United and Fulham Under-21s and returned to action away at Notts County last weekend.

The Boro would put a fifth three-point haul of the campaign on the board in that contest, as it looked set to end goalless only for Josh Magennis to break the deadlock four minutes from time.

Now sat 14th on 19 points, but just four points off the playoff spots with at least one game in hand on every team above them, Stevenage do have the chance to put themselves in a strong position if they can build on Saturday's win in the next few outings.

That will be no easy task, though, as the visitors arrive aiming to continue a perfect start to life under newly introduced management in the league.

Sheffield Wednesday arrived in League One, albeit on the back of relegation and administration last time around, with fresh optimism, a new-look squad and ownership and hopes to bounce back to the second tier at the first time of asking, and after a fast start, manager Henrik Pedersen's tenure would end with consecutive defeats to Notts County and Doncaster Rovers.

A pair of draws followed before the club hierarchy turned to Dave Challinor, whose tenure begun with back-to-back cup defeats to Oldham Athletic and Accrington Stanley.

It is clear their priorities lie with the league, though, and he has overseen victories in his first two third-tier matches at the helm, as the Owls firstly beat fellow promotion-chasers Plymouth Argyle 3-0 at Hillsborough before visiting Barnsley in a South Yorkshire Derby on Friday and winning 2-1 thanks to Jamal Lowe's first-half brace.

That leaves them fifth with momentum back on their side and just a three-point gap to second spot, and Sheffield Wednesday will now bid to make it three wins in three League One games under Challinor to further ramp up the pressure on the automatic promotion places.

Stevenage form (all competitions):.

Sheffield Wednesday League One form:.

Sheffield Wednesday form (all competitions):.

Stevenage will remain without Jasper Pattenden, Dan Kemp and Jordan Roberts on Tuesday due to ongoing injuries.

Revell should field a similar starting XI from the weekend's away win, although Magennis will likely return from the outset having won that game off the bench with his fourth League One goal of the season having also recorded four assists as their focal point.

He could be joined in a front two by Michael Mellon, who has seven goals in all competitions in the absence of supporting midfielder Kemp, while Louis Thompson and Daniel Phillips will continue their midfield partnership having been regulars this term after several major departures for the Boro over the summer.

Sheffield Wednesday could be unchanged from their victory on Friday, with Reece James, Max Lowe, Tyler Onyango, Mason Burstow and Ali Al-Hamadi likely to miss out again through injury.

Their injury troubles have eased recently, though, with Joe Lumley, Liam Cooper, Di'Shon Bernard, Billy Mitchell and Louie Barry all available after layoffs, and Cooper and Bernard will continue to play in a back three.

The absence of Lowe and James leaves a gap at left wing-back, while forward Jamal Lowe has filled in recent games, netting a brace on Friday, while Barry Bannan and Callum Slattery should again support front man Davis Keillor-Dunn with Barry continuing to be eased back after a lengthy spell in the treatment room.

Stevenage possible starting lineup:.

Setford; James-Wildin, Casey, Piergianni, Earley; Sanderson, Thompson, Phillips, Patterson; Mellon, Magennis.

Sheffield Wednesday possible starting lineup:.

Lumley; Bernard, Cooper, Swinkels, Valery, Heskey, Mitchell, J Lowe; Slattery, Bannan; Keillor-Dunn.

Stevenage head into Tuesday's game in better shape than their league position suggests and are always difficult to beat, having only conceded 13 league goals this term.

Sheffield Wednesday are growing into life under Challinor, though, and are beginning to show the quality that their squad is packed with, particularly with several important players back to full fitness, and we fancy them to make it three straight wins in a hard-fought away trip.

Match gallery: Bognor Regis Town Women too hot for AFC Varsity

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (617 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bognor took the lead on three minutes as Carter set up Hunphrey on the wing and she placed it low to Delillis, who diverted it in at the near post.
  • Sources indicate that alice Gue was fouled outside the area.
  • Nicole Robinson had to stop Dot Usher’s attempt at the other end.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bognor took the lead on three minutes as Carter set up Hunphrey on the wing and she placed it low to Delillis, who diverted it in at the near post.

Sources indicate that alice Gue was fouled outside the area. Up stepped Niamh Andersson to take the free-kick but she sent it just over.

Nicole Robinson had to stop Dot Usher’s attempt at the other end. Then Carter squared the ball towards Freya Boxer but she was put off by a defender.

Boxer spotted the keeper off her line and struck it from the far right but it rolled wide. Bognor had to defend with Usher causing problems and two strikes led to two good saves from Robinson.

Bognor extended their lead on 13 minutes as a defence-splitting pass set up Humphrey and she timed her run well before blasting it high into the net.

Sources indicate that carter had two long range efforts that bounced wide soon after. Lou Selvester's 22nd minute corner dipped into the heart of the area but Delillis couldn't quite control it and Lottie Tough gathered it.

Usher hit the Rockettes on the break and put in a perfect pass for Freya Lines who sped through the middle but her strike was well saved by Robinson.

Industry observers note that humphrey ran through and unselfishly played it across the box for Boxer to have a go but she struck it wide. Sophia Poling was late in a tackle on the left flank and was shown a yellow card in first half stoppage time.

Industry observers note that early in the second half, Andersson had a shot from long distance but that flew wide. Aliyah Bower hit the side netting from outside the box on 50 minutes at the other end. Delillis had the ball in the net after Carter's through ball but was ruled offside. Macie Downs won a corner with her long throw into the box but a Varsity defender headed away.

Lou Lou Robson came on for Sophia Poling and soon had to head a corner clear before Jess Nunn's strike was saved by Robinson.

Bognor got their third on 63 minutes as Delillis played a pass through defence to Humphrey and she ran into the box and sent the ball to the back post where Carter was waiting to smash it in.

It has been revealed that abbie Akhopie hit a dangerous cross into the area and Robinson had to save before Carter cleared the rebound. Clara Castanheira replaced Gue for the Rockettes then Andersson set up Boxer, but with only the keeper to beat, she fired wide.

Selvester's corner fell to Delillis and she struck the crossbar before Andersson smashed wide on the follow-up.

Bognor concede on 75 minutes as Akhopie sped through following a long ball and fired it in. Soon Delillis played it inside for Humphrey who turned and composed herself but shot wide.

According to recent reports, bower hit a long range free-kick at goal but Robinson denied her. On 80 minutes Poppy Shine replaced Robinson in goal for Bognor. Then on 83 minutes, Boxer came off for Talliah Anderson.

On 93 minutes Andersson came off for Chloe Blanks in Bognor's final change.

Bognor’s win leaves them second, three points behind leaders Havant with a game in hand.

The Rockettes travel to AFC Portchester Reserves on Sunday (November 29, 2pm) before welcoming Guernsey to Nyewood Lane on Sunday, December 6 (1pm).

Industry observers note that limitless started the brighter, dominating possession in the opening 10 minutes of this Sussex Junior Cup third round tie, before Goring gradually took control of the game with the midfield trio of Todor Bankov, Nathan Madgwick and Bambo carving out several chances for a front three of Connor Pomeroy, Ben Rubano and Luke Tate. Limitless kept Goring at bay until the 31st minute when Bambo fed Rubano whose clever flick found man of the match Connor Pomeroy who drove home from the edge of the box to give Goring a 1-0 lead. Four minutes later Bambo slipped in Pomeroy and his one two with Rubano saw him drive home for 2-0.

On 43 minutes a fine pass from Bankov found Pomeroy and his shot from just inside the box was very well saved by the home keeper. From the resultant corner, Luke Tate found Rubano who curled a delightful shot into the top corner to give Goring a well deserved 3-0 lead at half time.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Goring started the second half strongly with a Pomeroy header hitting the post on 48 minutes and a fine half volley soon after from Connor Harvey striking the crossbar. Debutant Josh Etherington went close on 63 minutes with a header from a Jacob Pippen cross before Limitless reduced the deficit from a free kick on 80 minutes, but the Goring defence of Ben Crack, Alex Staines, Charlie Sparks and Hayden Briggs were in no mood to concede again and the game ended with a well deserved 3-1 win for Goring who now go to Bosham Reserves for a fourth round tie on the 5th December.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Nolan | 23 Nov 2026 01:51.
  • Tottenham Hotspur are keeping tabs on Inter Milan striker Francesco Pio Esposito and Porto centre-forward Samu Omorodion, the latest report has claimed.
  • The Londoners continued their strong form on Saturday, emerging as 2-0 winners against Ipswich Town, claiming victory for the fourth time in five top-flight games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 23 Nov 2026 01:51.

Tottenham Hotspur are keeping tabs on Inter Milan striker Francesco Pio Esposito and Porto centre-forward Samu Omorodion, the latest report has claimed.

The Londoners continued their strong form on Saturday, emerging as 2-0 winners against Ipswich Town, claiming victory for the fourth time in five top-flight games.

Roberto De Zerbi's side are now ninth in the Premier League table with 15 points, and there are hope that the team can push for a European spot.

However, it will be a concern to the head coach that his team have only scored 12 goals in their 11 league fixtures.

It comes as no surprise to see Tottenham linked to both Inter's Esposito and Porto's Omorodion by reputable insider szyexcl on X (formerly Twitter), though they add that it is not clear if they will make a move for either player in January.

Esposito has enjoyed a fine season in Italy with Inter, scoring seven goals and providing one assist in just 767 minutes of football in all competitions.

The 21-year-old has proven himself to be deadly in the penalty area, with all six of his goals in Serie A coming from the middle of the box, though he would arguably be reliant on service from Tottenham's creators.

Omorodion has only played 310 minutes for Porto this season, finding the back of the net twice in that time, but there are concerns about how the 22-year-old would adapt to playing at the highest level in England.

While the striker has often performed well in Portugal, the likes of Darwin Nunez and Viktor Gyokeres struggled to bring their best form over to the Premier League, and it would be understandable if figures at Spurs were wary.

The fact that Tottenham are still in a position where they need significant changes in attack is damning given they spent more than £350m in the summer.

Forwards Omar Marmoush and Savio were both signed, but the former has only scored once in the league this season, while the latter is yet to find the back of the net.

Striker Solanke is the team's leading scorer in the top flight with two goals, though it would be wrong to suggest that he has played well this campaign.

Spurs may be in better form, but if they want to sustain a push for a place in Europe, they must strengthen their forward line.

Thomas Blake was replaced by James Henry for the visitors, and a Bello bomb of a throw was launched after Pattenden battled with O’Loughlin, although Dickinson collected at the second time of asking.

Chebby came on for Jeanes as Miles Rutherford and co rejigged, and Bello dropped back into defence.

The Chi sub was outmuscled by D’Andre Brown, and a penalty claim on Stoke sub Cheick Sylla was waved away by the referee.

Munt replaced Moore and a header from Clarke was deflected for a City corner.

Evans saved a speculative effort from long distance at the other end and somehow denied Henry with a brilliant save as we entered five extra minutes.

Chinedu Agu was booked for pulling back Huthchings and Bello did well to prevent Agu getting in on 93 minutes.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite another brace for a red-hot Nicole Mackay, Worthing Women were edged out in a five-goal ding-dong at Eastbourne Borough.

According to recent reports, there was some good news pre-match with the return of Captain Holly Talbut-Smith, in the only change to the starting line-up from last week’s win over Aylesford. Kendall Varitek also came back in for Ludmila De Sousa on the bench.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Aiming to build on three precious points achieved at home the previous Sunday, the Rebels travelled East to the Connect Management Stadium to face bottom-of-the-table Borough, although it was the struggling hosts who almost caught their guests by surprise in under a minute. Isobel Langridge sent in a cross that had goalkeeper Sian Woods backtracking to palm the ball to safety.

Moments later, the visitors retaliated by way of Neve McEvaddy releasing the nippy Jess Richardson through the inside-right channel who, in turn, picked out Nicole Mackay for a shot which flashed across the face of goal.

The same player went close again when a lucky break in the box failed to extend to Mackay, as her effort went wide once more.

However, Worthing’s number nineteen wouldn't be denied for much longer.

Richardson won a free-kick in a central position around twenty yards from goal and up stepped the Red’s top scorer to fire home the set-piece via a deflection, which wrong-footed Sophia Moule between the home posts.

The lead was nearly doubled shortly afterwards, only for the crossbar to keep out Mackay following a flicked header applied to a deadball delivery from McEvaddy.

Borough bit back via a misplaced pass providing an opening for Langridge to land a long ranger on top of the net, around the half-hour mark.

Then some excellent defending by first, returning Skipper Talbut-Smith resulted in Molly Hill being ushered away from the target, allowing netminder Woods to pounce on the ball and complete the clean up operation.

A presentable chance offered an opportunity to an unmarked Richardson in the penalty area in the closing stages of the first forty-five, though the fleet-footed winger couldn’t keep her attempt down.

McEvaddy was forced off at the break, to be replaced by Varitek but it would be the Reds of Eastbourne Borough who came out of the blocks quickest after the turnaround.

A mere three minutes into the second-half, Lola Dulake located the dome of Hill, who offered Worthing a possible mountain to climb by heading home to level the score.

Steepness then nearly became the order of the day, thanks to Hill coming mighty close to doubling her tally and putting her side in front within a matter of seconds.

Showing no signs of letting up, Hill, who else ? was inches away again when she put a good chance over the apparatus, before the deadly duo of Dulake and Hill linked up to devastating effect to extend the homesters’ advantage, just shy of the hour.

The former crossed from the right and the latter gleefully gobbled up the opportunity to nod in her brace.

Roles were slightly reversed at the point Duklake fizzed a low attempt dangerously close to the target and Woods was called into action to repel a close-range effort, as the home team threatened to pull clear of their beleaguered opponents.

Dulake turned Ella Terry but could only find the hands of Woods, by which time Skye Birkinshaw had entered the fray in place of youngster Hattie Rainey, as Manager Jesus Cordon and his Coaching Staff tried to find a way back into the contest for the underfire travellers.

Fellow substitute Daisy Taylor almost had the opposite effect, as her long distance rocket forced a fine diving save out of Woods, at the expense of a corner.

A through ball might have put the game beyond Worthing’s reach, had Woods not had her wits about her to race out of her goal to intercept and smother at the feet of the hat-trick hunting Hill.

Six minutes from the end of ninety, Hill claimed the matchball by getting the better of Terry and gaining added purchase on an effort which crashed off the underside of the crossbar and fell the right slide of the line, for Borough.

Not letting their heads drop though, Rebels let out a yell when Mackay made it five goals in her last three games, as she swivelled on the edge of the eighteen yard box to beat Moule and set up a tense conclusion.

Unfortunately however, three-two to an understandably elated Eastbourne saw them collect only their second league win of the campaign, although, with just four points separating the bottom five clubs, nobody is safe.

By Lewis Nolan | 23 Nov 2026 03:17.

Manchester City could bring Enzo Fernandez back into their starting XI on Tuesday, when they face Napoli in the Champions League.

The midfielder started on the bench when the Citizens faced Fulham on Saturday, with the Argentine having received criticism for his poor defensive displays.

However, it may be unrealistic to expect teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi to start once again, so perhaps Fernandez will partner Elliot Anderson in a double pivot.

Antoine Semenyo's knee injury will keep him out of Tuesday's clash, meaning fans are likely to see Iliman Ndiaye and Jeremy Doku stationed out wide in attack.

Rayan Cherki is set to come back into the team in favour of Phil Foden, and the Frenchman will be tasked with supporting striker Erling Haaland.

Should right-back Matheus Nunes miss out, it would not be surprising to see Enzo Maresca play Abdukodir Khusanov on that side of the backline.

Ruben Dias, Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol are candidates to start in the other three positions in defence, while goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma can be pencilled into the lineup.

Manchester City possible starting lineup:.

Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Fernandez; Ndiaye, Cherki, Doku; Haaland.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The club stalwart has been put in temporary chatge at The Saffrons while the club look for a permanent replacement for Macdonald, whose axing alongside assistant Ben Davis has provoked an angry reaction from many fans and seen some players leave – includihg one who’d only rejoined the club on Friday.

The latest development at the Isthmian South East club came on Monday evening, when a club statement remarked: “To serve for an interim period, Eastbourne Town F.C are pleased to announce the appointment of popular club stalwart Dave Winterton as First Team Manager.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

"Dave is, of course, very well known to most people in the local area for his long and distinguished playing, coaching and management career with our club, and we sincerely thank him for agreeing to take on this role.

"During this time, Dave will be assisted by one of our experienced senior players, Arron Hopkinson. Our thanks also go to him.

"We hope that supporters will get behind Dave and the team during this period of transition, starting this coming Saturday away at Erith Town, whilst the search for a permanent successor to Jude Macdonald continues.”.

Dave is a second generation Winterton at Eastbourne Town – his father Derek played as a defender for the club in the 1950s.

Industry observers note that he was club manager between June 2001 and January 2005, taking Town, who were playing in Division 2 of the Sussex League, into Division 1 and winning the Sussex Intermediate Cup. In 2020 Dave became the Goalkeeper coach for the club.

The move to make him interim boss comes after the surprise news on Saturday evening that Macdonald had been sacked with Town one off the bottom of the division but after two brighter league performances that had seen a point taken from each of two clashes with Sheppey and Whitstable.

Town’s statement on Saturday remarked: “Eastbourne Town FC have today parted company with First Team Manager Jude Macdonald and Ben Davis.

"The Committee would like to place on record their sincere thanks to Jude and Ben for their hard work over the last 4½ years, where, following their arrival, they quickly reshaped the remaining playing squad, and with some exciting newly introduced arrivals, just two years later rolled out an amazing mid-season recovery to storm up the SCFL Premier Division table to finish Runners-Up and then win the League Play-off Final.

"They then successfully kept the Club in the Isthmian F.L for successive seasons when largely up against many teams with much greater budgets and resources, a feat which we believe must be seen as a remarkable achievement in what is known by many to be a very tough division.

Sources indicate that "The club wish them both all the very best for the future and thank them once again for their service during their time at The Saffrons. No further statements will be made at this time.”.

A number of Town fans have taken to social media to condemn Macdonald’s removal, calling it shocking and disgraceful.

At least a couple of players have left – including James Waters, who Macdonald had re-signed for the club only at the end of last week.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 17:25 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 17:35 EST, 21 November 2026.

Wouter Vrancken noted Hearts’ ruthless 8-0 demolition of 10-man Dundee was his team’s best performance since he took charge at Tynecastle.

Sabah Kerjota and Pierre Landry Kabore both scored twice with Claudio Braga, Sabri Guendouz, Stuart Findlay and a Ryan Finnigan own goal taking the tally to eight without reply.

And Vrancken was naturally delighted that his players had ended a run of three defeats in a row in such spectacular style.

Sources indicate that the 47-year-old said: 'The best performance? Of course.

'When you have the confidence of one moment and then you feel the score is getting bigger, you see the players with extra confidence.

'You see the dynamics there and it’s good they feel it works.

Stuart Findlay heads in the eighth to cap a remarkable evening for Hearts at Dens Park.

'When it’s 0-0 and 1-0, you don’t feel as confident so maybe you don’t have the bravery to do it or show it.

'Today they did it and hopefully they felt it can work and they can show it more.

'It was ruthless and I like to see it this way. That was the message at half-time – that and keeping the clean sheet.

'I was very happy with the performance, not only the score.

'We had the talks before our days off, they were really honest and open. It was good to hear but you have to take ownership of it on the pitch.

'You can talk as much as you want but if you can’t show it on the pitch it doesn’t mean anything.

'When you do it like this it’s the first step.

'But it’s only the first step, only one game and we have to try to bring more.

“The message to the players is feet back on the ground because after the last break we started with a 5-0 win over St Mirren then had difficult moments.

'It was ruthless in the game today but the schedule is also ruthless – but we got a good boost from tonight.'.

Claudio Braga fires home a fifth goal for Vrancken's side in the demolition job.

Dundee boss Steven Pressley admitted he was embarrassed by the result and performance.

According to recent reports, he said: 'It’s a night I need to own, a night where I can only apologise for the performance. I never expected that.

'I had a little sense we haven’t been quite on it over the last couple of weeks but I take ownership and I mean that.

'We talk about the culture and environment that we set and part of that is making sure we have a fully motivated team, a team which works hard and highlights grit.

'We didn’t show that tonight but that is on me and I mean that.

'We looked unmotivated and lacking edge tonight.

'Tactically astute, we were miles away and that’s my responsibility.

'All areas of our performance was disappointing.

'I’m embarrassed by it and I accept it.'.

Painful Coventry defeat will send shudder of fear through Newcastle

📅 13 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 22 min read (4447 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~22 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.
  • It was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game.
  • Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

It was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

Recent findings suggest that matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”.

Industry observers note that matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8.

Newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

“It was an outstanding performance,” the manager said. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”.

The win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

Industry observers note that as for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. It also means people will query whether Jaissle’s implementation of “vertical football” is working. The fact Lampard talked so openly about winning the duels to set up the win will anger the German.

Jaissle can point to two bad misses from one of the latest arrivals, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a £51m buy from Lille, in the first half. But his team are too easy to play through and the defence is an accident waiting to happen.

Industry observers note that even after Sven Botman’s stunning strike offered them a way back into the game, they capitulated at the back as Lewis Hall – who was off colour all evening – and Joelinton’s mistakes gift-wrapped a third for Ellis Simms. A fourth followed for Stephen Mfuni.

Ellis Simms off the bench with a big impact! 💥 https://t.co/XynFVxwERV.

Industry observers note that you can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

Sources indicate that it was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

Recent findings suggest that nico González spotted the run of Fernandez-Pardo through the middle. He wriggled clear of Bobby Thomas and sat down goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, but the Coventry centre-back got back to block his shot.

It has been revealed that newcastle pressed the self-destruct button early in the second half. A long throw into the box was half cleared. There was a half-hearted attempt to close Cherif down from Yoane Wissa and then a shot that somehow went through a crowd of three Newcastle defenders, including the legs of Botman, and nestled in the bottom corner.

Sidiki Cherif with a STUNNING finish on his first Premier League start! 🤩 https://t.co/EoTB8VCHuR.

It should have been three. Again Wissa was partly to blame, losing the ball in midfield to set Coventry on the counter-attack. When Botman made a mess of a clearance it spun perfectly into the path of Cherif. The net should have bulged but the £20m summer signing from Fenerbahce scuffed wide.

The visitors needed something special to get back into it and it came from the most unlikely of sources as Botman unleashed a rocket from 25 yards.

Industry observers note that sven Botman, that is SENSATIONAL! 🤯 https://t.co/GalkqMs5ZE.

Recent findings suggest that in a flash the balance of play shifted in Newcastle’s favour. They poured forward in search of the equaliser. Jaissle switched to a 4-4-2 with Will Osula joining Fernandez-Pardo up front, but instead of pulling level, Coventry pulled further ahead.

"We need to improve the things we can control, and right now that's a lot" 🗣️ Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle expresses his disappointment after his side's loss to Coventry 👇 https://t.co/fatJkZYyRM.

Sources indicate that very, very satisfying. It’s so hard to win. We played like the team we want to be here. A team you look at and go there’s so much energy and spirit in the group. We know we are going to have to suffer this season, when we don’t have a lot of the ball. We have to understand it. The level is what it is.

In a recent development, the work ethic, the belief. You get what you deserve. Great finishes. We haven’t quite had the rub of the green this season and that might have helped us nick a couple of more points. I’m a firm believer that you keep going. It was a complete performance. We’ve got to keep our feet on the ground because we’re going to have to do 30+ of those but it’s a great feeling for the players.

Recent findings suggest that [Cherif] is very, very exciting because he is so young. He has got a really good manner. He wants to train, he wants to learn. He’s quite quiet but on the pitch he shows a lot of personality. When you see the quality of the strike and the hold-up play, there’s a lot to come from him.

"That one was for you, nan" Jack Rudoni explains his goal celebration ❤️ https://t.co/79OvHMlu6J.

A victory to savour for Coventry whose teenagers Cherif and Mfuni scored fine goals. No doubt they wobbled when Botman equalised and for the next 10 minutes but Newcastle blew too many chances and resumed making errors at the back. Newcastle’s squad is a mess.

Newcastle might maintain that Thomas-Asante was offside and blocking the keeper’s view when Mfuni pulled the trigger but I think Hornicke had a clear view and hence it wasn’t an offence.

The first two minutes of stoppage time, of which there are four, pass without incident.

Osula lifts a volley over the bar with a wild attempt. Toure was injured in the build-up and will be replaced by Dan Burn.

According to recent reports, never mind Bob Gelodof and Brenda Ann Spencer, Matthias Jaissle doesn’t like Mondays. They are 8-2 down on Monday Night Football so far this season.

Coventry 4 Newcastle 1 (Mfuni) The substitute had only just replaced Rudoni and took the ball on the inside-left 25 yards out, advanced then wrapped his instep around a left-foot shot, arrowing it across Hornicek into the bottom right.

Stephen Mfuni makes his mark for Coventry! 👊 https://t.co/KI2kgpfUJP.

Recent findings suggest that thomas-Asante crashes a right-foot shot into the heart of the left post. A thumping strike that leaves the metalwork ringing.

Coventry 3 Newcastle 1 (Simms) Right foot shot from 18 yards through Thiaw’s legs, clipping the inside of his right knee to deflect it into the bottom left. Joelinton had been trying to dribble it out of the box, overhit it and fouled Thomas-Asante as he tried to recover. The whistle was betweeen the ref’s lips but he did not exhale as Simms steered his shot through Thiaw’s legs.

Industry observers note that ellis Simms off the bench with a substantial impact! 💥 https://t.co/XynFVxwERV.

Sources indicate that touré beats Dasilva for pace down the right then blazes over from a tight angle then moments later is given an opportunity to shoot and sticks it in the stands again. Both times the cross was on.

Toure has caused untold problems for Dasilva. Newcastle corner on the left is bent far too deep and goes out for a goal-kick.

Onyeka → YirenkyiSimms → Cherif.

Wissa dithers over a shot when found by Toure to the right of the penalty spot and finally clips it into Thomas. Coventry are clinging on but flapping. As is the crowd.

Hall, following Botman’s lead, lets fly from distance, straight at Rushworth.

Coventry fluff a couple of chances to break with hasty, panicked passes.

It was as if Coventry were defying him to have a shot. And in doing so, the nerves are back with a bang in the crowd.

According to recent reports, coventry 2 Newcastle 1 (Botman) Coventry invite him to shoot by backing off and backing off and he RSVPs with a left-foot torpedo from 20 yards into the roof of the net. What a strike!

Sven Botman, that is SENSATIONAL! 🤯 https://t.co/GalkqMs5ZE.

Industry observers note that barnes appears to have been brought down by Sakamoto in the Coventry penalty area but he was offside. One of Jaissle’s staff is booked for some verbal transgression.

Joelinto rattles bones in a tackle that was not shown as they focus on Barnes’ spurious penalty appeal when he slipped behind Pinnock.

Rudoni dips his shoulder and skins Botman in the Newcastle box but tries and fails to square it to Cherif instead of shooting.

Industry observers note that touré makes ground down the right and slips Joelinton down the inside. The substitute, who took the captain’s armband off Thiaw, tries to find Pardo with a cross that Thomas blocks.

Now Willock blazes over from eight yards on the right after a slick one-two with Murphy.

Dedic → MileyTouré → MurphyJoelinton → Willock.

Rushworth drops Hall’s cross but recovers to grab it on the bounce. Jaissle has three subs stripped. Murphy tries to bend a cross from the right to Barnes at the back post but Van Ewijk and Thomas combine to scramble it out for a throw-in.

It has been revealed that now Cherif misses a gilded opportunity after a hacked clearance from Botman lands at his feet to the left of the spot. He kicks it into his other leg and the ball dribbles wide. The way Botman dealt with Thomas-Asante’s cross was really shoddy.

Sources indicate that barnes disguises his inside run and evades Van Ewijk to collect Thiaw’s pass up the inside-right channel. He spins and feeds it infield to Wissa who telegraphs his shot with a laboured touch before swiinging a right-footer from 25 yards straight down Rushworth’s throat.

Newcastle have been awful. Seem to lack leadership and heft on the field. The return of Joelinton can’t come quick enough.

Coventry 2 Newcastle 0 (Cherif) Talented lad. Absolutely larrups a right-foot shot through a thicket of Newcastle legs from 18 yards when a long throw was headed out to the edge of the box.

Industry observers note that sidiki Cherif with a STUNNING finish on his first Premier League start! 🤩 https://t.co/EoTB8VCHuR.

It has been revealed that collison between Van Ewijk and Willock leaves them both winded and needing treatment. The Newcastle midfielder had been trying to bullock down the middle in purusit of a pass.

Coventry overload with seven men on the right before rolling the kick-off to the left-footed Rushworth who rolls out it too far up that wing and Hornicek gathers.

Interesting half for Matias Fernandez-Pardo who has been in the middle of most of Newcastle’s best moments but has failed to take two excellent chances.

It has been revealed that the first was baffling as the Belgium international made no attempt to sweep in Jacob Murphy’s cutback at the near post, letting it run through his legs thinking Harvey Barnes was in a better position. He wasn’t.

The second was a little unfortunate as he did well to time his run and wriggle free of centre back Bobby Thomas. That put him in on goal with just the goalkeeper to beat, but having sat Chris Rushworth down he pushed the ball a fraction too wide and by the time he was in a position to shoot, Thomas had done brilliantly to cut off the angle and block it.

Coventry have been good but Newcastle have been really poor again away from home. They are yet to put a 90-minute performance together since the opening weekend against Liverpool. Matthias Jaissle will want a lot more from his team in the second half.

Newcastle should at least be level given their chances but you have to admire Coventry’s spirit and work rate. Cherif seems to me to have a high ceiling and at 19 is already a real handful.

In a recent development, newcastle need to stop fannying around and buy a proper centre-forward. Wissa is better wide or in a more fluid system, as I suspect Fernandez-Pardo is, too. Stick Osula on and get the chequebook out in January. Offer Boro £50m for Lankshear.

Cheeif, working his socks off, chases a lost cause and retrieves a long pass forward in the whitewash but when he turns to try to play it to Thomas-Asante, Thiaw makes a good tackle.
